question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{4}+1 \\ {x}^{3}y-3\end{aligned}]. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}.$
${x}_{1}=[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{4}+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{4}+1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}y-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}y-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & -4{y}^{3} \\ 3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -4{y}^{3} \\ 3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{4}+1 \\ {x}^{3}y-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & -4{y}^{3} \\ 3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{4}+1 \\ {x}^{3}y-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(1) & -4(1)^{3} \\ 3(1)^{2}(1) & (1)^{3}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}-(1)^{4}+1 \\ (1)^{3}(1)-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2\cdot 1-(-4)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
